1. Executive summary

1.1 Shared vision and ambition for the place

Partners wish to collaborate on area-based regeneration solutions, to maximise and align government and other public and private funding, investment and support, to enhance locally-led housing growth and regeneration.

This Place Delivery Agreement (PDA) between South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority, Homes England (the trading name of Homes and Communities Agency) and National Housing Bank Limited is dated 30 October 2026 and strengthens the relationship between South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority (SYMCA), Homes England and the National Housing Bank (NHB) through an enhanced single delivery framework to accelerate housing delivery, unlock regeneration and underpin South Yorkshire’s Growth Plan ambition for a bigger and better South Yorkshire economy.

Building on the success of the existing Strategic Place Partnership (SPP), this agreement represents a step change in the way the 3 organisations work together. It moves beyond collaboration towards co-delivery, bringing together local leadership, national expertise and investment capability behind a shared set of priorities.

At its heart, the Agreement is about empowering the Mayor and local leaders to deliver their housing, regeneration and growth ambitions by bringing decision-making, investment and delivery capability closer to place.

Through this Agreement, the partners commit to the following:

1.2 Strategic partnership objectives

Develop and deliver a robust pipeline of investment-ready proposals to unlock and accelerate housing delivery across South Yorkshire.

Increase the supply of high quality, energy efficient and affordable homes to meet the region’s housing needs, including an enhanced council and social house building programme given all 4 local authorities are stock holding. Housing Associations will be supported through working with the South Yorkshire Housing Partnership.

Support local areas in developing their area-based growth and regeneration solutions around places — triggered by Catalyst Sites, providing opportunities to create and grow sustainable neighbourhoods and supporting the region’s economic growth and inclusivity objectives.

1.3 Headline outcomes sought

Closer joint working between Homes England and SYMCA to support communities across the region which are in need of a package of regeneration activities and investment including demolitions, new infrastructure, new housing, and environmental improvements to achieve better-quality homes and places that improve the health, wellbeing and prosperity of those communities.

An early focus will see the delivery of 5,550 new homes across 8 Catalyst Sites, plus accompanying employment and residential development across the Don Valley Corridor.

A pipeline of development-ready public land to accelerate delivery of housing for social and affordable rent.

Empowering SYMCA to shape housing investment and delivery priorities across all tenures.

Supporting mayoral influence over social and affordable housing investment decisions through regionally delegated Social and Affordable Housing Programme (SAHP) Continuous Market Engagement (CME) arrangements.

Aligning Homes England and National Housing Bank activity with the South Yorkshire Growth Plan, levering other investment and supporting placemaking.

1.4 Key delivery priorities

Early priorities will focus upon the delivery of 5 of the 8 Catalyst Sites: Furnace Hill and Neepsend (Sheffield), Moorfoot (Sheffield), Hoyland North and South (Barnsley), Unity (Doncaster) and Bassingthorpe Farm (Rotherham), along with near-term wins within the Don Valley Corridor area. These priorities have been identified in partnership with each of the local authorities.

Emerging priorities will focus upon:

(i) a refresh of the South Yorkshire Housing Pipeline with an emphasis on interrogating opportunities that may arise from public land

(ii) firming up the South Yorkshire Integrated Affordable Homes Programme, with a fresh look at opportunities arising from council delivery

(iii) Phase 2 Catalyst Sites including:

Carlton and Royston (Barnsley)

Doncaster Waterfront and City Centre (Doncaster)

Town Centre and Riverside (Rotherham)

Accelerating social and affordable housing and council house delivery:

ensuring the delivery of the mayoral ambition for around 9,000 new affordable and council homes across South Yorkshire from 2026 to 2031

maximising the impact of South Yorkshire’s £700 million SAHP indicative spend amount

supporting local authorities, registered providers and delivery partners to enhance, prioritise and deliver the existing South Yorkshire Housing Pipeline

remediating and preparing a pipeline of land (particularly public land) to development readiness

1.5 Commitment to joint working

The agency’s service offer to SYMCA as an Established Mayoral Strategic Authority (EMSA) concerns the delivery capabilities (people resource) Homes England will provide to SYMCA to help shape housing and regeneration delivery locally based upon agreed delivery principles. These will be deployed through a Joint Delivery Unit (JDU) co-located with SYMCA and which, together with SYMCA capacity, will form a Joint Delivery Team (JDT).

The offer has 3 proposed elements:

a) core capabilities that will be embedded in the JDT for the “lifetime” of the partnership

b) project capabilities that can be drawn down for the JDT to resource project teams based on the long-term skillsets required

c) specialist capabilities that can be drawn down for JDT and project teams to meet a shorter-term task or project specific requirement

SYMCA and Homes England will also jointly explore new opportunities to develop their collective roles to bring forward more land to development readiness to support new housing, particularly public land to provide housing for social and affordable rent.

The JDT will work in partnership with each of the local authorities to deliver on this PDA, maximising the collective strengths of all partners.

1.6 Strengthening accountability and governance

Significantly enhanced accountability through a shared performance framework and direct reporting arrangements to the Mayor.

Establishing strengthened oversight arrangements involving the Mayor, the chairs of Homes England and the National Housing Bank and the chief executives of both organisations.

Delegating day-to-day Homes England and National Housing Bank responsibility for delivery of the Agreement to the Homes England executive director for the North East, Yorkshire and the Humber.

Nominated co-directors from SYMCA and Homes England will lead the JDT.

Introducing quarterly senior sponsor meetings to oversee delivery, resolve barriers and hold the partnership to account for agreed outcomes.

1.7 Commencement and term

This PDA shall commence on the signing date and shall continue for an initial period of 3 years (subject to an annual review) and shall continue for such further period or periods as shall be agreed in writing between the parties, Provided always that any party may give not less than 90 days prior written notice to the others to terminate this PDA at any time.

2. Place context and opportunity

2.1 Place overview

South Yorkshire is a region in the Yorkshire and the Humber region of Northern England.

It borders North Yorkshire and West Yorkshire to the north, the East Riding of Yorkshire to the north-east, Lincolnshire to the east, Nottinghamshire to the south-east, Derbyshire to the south, and Greater Manchester to the west. The largest settlement is the city of Sheffield.

The region comprises 4 distinct places:

Barnsley — the UK’s first Tech Town, enterprising market town traditions, strong communities

Doncaster — South Yorkshire’s gateway for rail and global connectivity; Airport City; a city of rich heritage, market towns and strong communities

Rotherham — Manufacturing excellence; innovation and engineering; world’s first Children’s Capital of Culture

Sheffield — Core city; universities and research; creative industries; advanced manufacturing leadership

The 4 local authorities of Barnsley, Doncaster, Rotherham, and Sheffield collaborate through the South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority to drive prosperity, housing and economic growth across the region.

South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority area map

The map shows the South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority area, covering Barnsley, Sheffield, Rotherham, Doncaster.

2.2 Growth ambitions

South Yorkshire’s Growth Plan runs from 2025 to 2035 and seeks to build a bigger and better South Yorkshire economy.

It states that over the next decade, SYMCA will coordinate and prioritise investment towards 4 priority Growth Areas to create secure, high-paid jobs, which bring income and further investment into the region.

Priority Growth Areas map

The map shows Barnsley town centre, Sheffield city centre and Innovation Spine, Don Valley and South Yorkshire Airport City.

8 Catalyst Sites have also been identified across the region which are housing-led regeneration priorities with the potential to deliver over 8,695 new homes. These are:

Hoyland North and South (Barnsley)

Royston and Carlton (Barnsley)

Unity (Doncaster)

Doncaster Waterfront and City Centre (Doncaster)

Bassingthorpe Farm (Rotherham)

Town Centre and Riverside and Gateway (Rotherham)

Moorfoot (Sheffield)

Furnace Hill and Neepsend (Sheffield)

2.3 Housing and regeneration challenges

Development-ready land availability

Homelessness, rough sleeping, and supported housing

Affordable housing

Affordability

Local authority capacity

Viability challenges

Specialist provision

Skills shortages in the construction and ‘green’ skills sectors

2.4 Market failures and barriers to delivery

Supply chain costs have risen substantially since 2020, and though they have stabilised, are the new reality.

New planning and building regulation policies have added to costs since 2021 and this is also part of the new reality.

Market housing values in the region are currently relatively subdued but with the housing market expected to improve over the next 12 months.

The viability of housebuilding in South Yorkshire is a significant issue on many urban brownfield sites.

In places there is the prevalence of contamination on brownfield sites due to the mining and heavy industrial heritage of the region.

There are also viability challenges on greenfield sites, including within the Green Belt, due to topography challenges and the costs of installing infrastructure.

Planning costs which can be varied locally may need to look to reflect regeneration priorities more closely.

2.5 Strategic opportunities

The housing aspiration for South Yorkshire is to ensure that everyone has access to good quality, warm homes that are affordable and meet needs, while helping achieve ambitions for a net zero economy and sustainable, attractive places to live, work and invest.

This aspiration maintains an emphasis on housing growth, with a focus particularly on supporting both regeneration and repurposing of city and town centres, as well as providing a stronger focus on decarbonising the existing housing stock and improving the design quality and environmental standards of homes for everyone.

Collectively, as of 2024, Local Plans estimated an affordable housing need of 2,000 homes for the region although we know this figure will be higher due to the latest Housing Needs Assessment in Sheffield in 2024 identifying a need for 2,000 in Sheffield alone. Although the region has been delivering around 5,000 new homes per annum, affordable homes built have only been around 20% of need. There is therefore both a need and an opportunity to address this historic undersupply of affordable housing across the region.

In some places within the region there is a lack of available brownfield housing opportunities, and so investment in greenfield housing schemes will also be required to meet regional housing needs.

There are significant opportunities, particularly in urban centres, not only for new housing but also for new commercial development and infrastructure to contribute to wider regeneration and renewal ambitions and help drive a net zero transition for places across South Yorkshire.

As all council social housing stock in the region is owned by the 4 local authorities, including 2 Arm’s-Length Management Organisations (ALMO) in Barnsley and Doncaster, there is a region-wide opportunity to deliver an enhanced council and social house build programme across South Yorkshire to meet the growing need for high-quality affordable housing.

There are homelessness needs across the region, particularly in the cities where further accommodation options and wrap-around support, including via the SAHP and our Homelessness Prevention and Supported Housing programmes will be needed.

SYMCA, the 4 South Yorkshire local authorities, housing associations and Homes England have joined up to form the South Yorkshire Housing Partnership (SYHP) to seek to ensure levels of house building are maintained, with a particular focus on affordable housing provision.

Housing delivery provides an opportunity for local job creation and skills development, especially through procurement and partnership.

2.6 Alignment with Mayor’s priorities, local growth plans and Homes England objectives

There is a close alignment between the Mayor’s priorities and those of Homes England, and both parties will work collaboratively and flexibly at all levels of their organisations to explore creative ways to deliver more affordable high-quality homes that will support economic growth and placemaking within South Yorkshire. This will include exploring new opportunities to develop their collective roles to bring forward more land to development readiness to support new housing, particularly public land and to provide housing for social and affordable rents.

The PDA will play a key role in seeking to deliver the SYMCA Integrated Settlement’s housing growth and regeneration outcomes, particularly in relation to the delivery of both the region’s National Housing Delivery Programme (NHDF) and the Social and Affordable Housing Programme (SAHP).

The local authorities of South Yorkshire will continue to be involved in influencing and shaping the emerging priorities.

3.3 Social and Affordable Housing and council house delivery

Affordable housing is one of the clearest examples of how this PDA will bring decision-making, delivery capability and accountability closer to place.

Through this Agreement, the JDT will ensure affordable housing investment is aligned with the Mayor’s priorities for growth, regeneration and housing delivery. By combining regional decision-making with dedicated delivery capability and specialist affordable housing expertise, the partnership will enable investment decisions to be shaped more directly by local priorities and delivery opportunities.

South Yorkshire has an indicative spend amount of £700 million through the SAHP, creating a significant opportunity to accelerate social and affordable housing and council house delivery across the region. Through the JDU, partners will work together to maximise the impact of this investment, increase the pace and scale of delivery, and ensure affordable housing investment supports wider regeneration, economic growth and placemaking ambitions.

Through this partnership, the parties will seek to facilitate the delivery of the Mayor’s ambition for around 9,000 new affordable and council homes across South Yorkshire from 2026 to 2031, including increasing broader regeneration and economic growth outcomes.

The partnership will maintain and enhance the South Yorkshire Housing Pipeline, ensuring activity and investment are directed towards opportunities that can unlock or accelerate delivery, address housing need and contribute to the ambitions of the South Yorkshire Growth Plan. This will include:

a) SAHP decisions on Continuous Market Engagement (CME) delegated.

These will be delegated to the regional SAHP team (within agreed thresholds) with the JDT providing the governance forum for approval to enable investment decisions to be locally led and determined.

b) The Mayor and SYMCA being given full visibility of the affordable housing pipeline data in their area.

Through the JDT and enhanced governance, they will be included in the affordable housing pipeline review and CME assessment process providing local insights and data to develop proposals.

c) The Mayor and SYMCA being involved in the assessment and decision-making process for further procurement rounds or extensions to existing Strategic Partnership allocations that affect the region.

d) A clearly-defined escalation process if members of the JDT cannot agree on the SAHP CME investment decision to be made, via the PDA and, or, JDT or respective governance structures for a definitive decision. This will be through monthly governance.

e) Working with Registered Provider Strategic Partners operating within the SAHP to align investment plans and develop a coordinated pipeline of social and affordable housing opportunities across the region, supporting delivery of the Mayor’s affordable housing and regeneration priorities.

Recognising the government’s ambition to significantly increase council house delivery, Homes England will support the SYMCA to:

review the barriers to delivery of council housing and work collaboratively with local authorities to implement the preferred approaches including the potential to align with other thematic areas including land, industrialised construction and other forms of investment

bring empty homes back into use and other improvements to existing stock including where there are positive links to be made to other policy areas such as reduced use of temporary accommodation

3.4 Public sector land

Working together to explore additional opportunities for land assembly and acquisitions, specifically opportunities for affordable housing delivery.

In addition, through the JDU supporting local authorities to bring sites forward for council and Registered Provider affordable housing delivery.

3.5 Place-based investment and finance

The delivery of South Yorkshire’s housing and regeneration ambitions will require investment at a scale that cannot be achieved through grant funding alone. Unlocking transformational opportunities will depend on the ability to combine public and private capital, recycle investment over time and develop investable propositions capable of attracting long-term institutional funding.

The National Housing Bank (NHB), launched by Homes England in 2026, has been established to accelerate the delivery of new homes and mixed-use regeneration schemes through flexible public investment. Backed by up to £16 billion of debt, equity and guarantee products, the bank is designed to work with national, regional and local partners to unlock housing delivery, crowd-in private capital and support the government’s ambition to deliver 1.5 million homes while delivering a positive financial return for the Exchequer.

SYMCA and Homes England share an ambition to use the PDA as a platform to develop innovative approaches to place-based investment, enhancing the existing pipeline of investable housing and regeneration opportunities and increasing the scale of private capital investment into the region.

As part of this Agreement, the National Housing Bank will actively seek opportunities to amplify the region’s local investment fund supporting housing and regeneration ambition and the Mayor’s priorities to attract wider investment using its lending, equity or guarantee capacity.

The National Housing Bank will support the development of a portfolio of investment opportunities capable of unlocking a significantly greater level of private and institutional capital investment over time, including from the NHB.

Partners will work together to identify and develop housing-led regeneration, infrastructure-enabled growth, mixed-use development and strategic land opportunities that have the potential to unlock significantly greater levels of private and institutional investment over time.

The partnership will seek to:

align National Housing Bank products and investment capabilities with mayoral growth and regeneration priorities

maximise the deployment of NHB products in South Yorkshire through targeted promotion, advice and support to the sector

crowd-in institutional and private-sector capital alongside public investment

explore innovative approaches to land, infrastructure and development finance that accelerate delivery and improve viability

The SYMCA allocation of the National Housing Accelerator Fund will operate alongside National Housing Bank investment activity, helping to address barriers to delivery and develop the investable pipeline required to attract future bank support. Together, these funding streams have the potential to create a flexible source of capital to unlock strategic housing and regeneration priorities across the region.

3.6 Skills and capacity for housing growth ambition

Delivering the scale of housing and regeneration envisaged by the Local Growth Plan will require sufficient development capacity, technical expertise and workforce skills across both the public and private sectors. Addressing these challenges is critical to accelerating housing delivery, supporting economic growth and ensuring South Yorkshire can maximise the opportunities presented by major regeneration and infrastructure investment.

Through this Agreement, Homes England and the South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority will work together to ensure that the skills, capacity, capability and innovation required to support long-term housing growth and regeneration are embedded across the region, creating the foundations for sustainable housing delivery and inclusive economic growth.

The Parties will support the development of construction skills pipelines, promote apprenticeships and employment opportunities. This will build on the ambitions set out in the South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority’s Skills Strategy, Housing Framework and Local Skills Improvement Plan.

The partnership will seek to:

align housing investment with South Yorkshire’s skills, employment and economic growth priorities, including the ambitions of the Skills Strategy and the ‘Get South Yorkshire Working’ programme

support delivery of South Yorkshire’s growth ambitions by strengthening the construction workforce, increasing productivity through modern methods of construction, digital technologies and innovative delivery approaches, and supporting the delivery of high-quality, sustainable homes across the region

identify and address skills shortages within construction occupations that may impact the delivery of strategic housing and regeneration sites, informed by the South Yorkshire Local Skills Improvement Plan and employer-led evidence on workforce demand

support the development of a skilled construction and built-environment workforce through collaboration with local authorities, employers, training providers, further and higher education institutions, and industry partners

share labour market intelligence, housing delivery data and emerging evidence on workforce needs to inform future skills provision, investment decisions and long-term delivery planning

4. Joint delivery and governance framework

4.1 Partnership commitments

This new single framework will help to strengthen local capability to support delivery, while recognising a desire to go further in boosting the capacity, expertise and sharing of good practice across the public and private sector partners in the sub-region via a focused programme of activity.

The JDT will provide greater visibility and accountability to the Mayor, giving the Mayor the control, influence and resources needed to build the homes and places communities require and to hold partners to account for delivery.

Homes England, National Housing Bank and the South Yorkshire Mayoral Combined Authority commit to seeking to work as a single team utilising our resources, skills and capabilities to achieve our shared outcomes for the region by:

aligning resources around agreed shared priorities

maintaining a shared development and investment pipeline

jointly identifying and resolving barriers

coordinating stakeholder engagement

sharing intelligence and investment planning

supporting delivery through an embedded and dedicated Joint Delivery Team

progressing new joint activities to bring forward a pipeline of land to development readiness for social and affordable housing

progressing a joint Delivery Plan outlining key tasks, milestones and resourcing commitments underpinned by a governance framework which delivers on the principles outlined in this PDA

This PDA will operate on a 3-year basis and will be reviewed annually to ensure it remains aligned with evolving national policy, mayoral priorities, market conditions and delivery opportunities. The PDA is intended to provide a single framework while retaining sufficient flexibility to respond to changing circumstances and emerging priorities.

Delivery of the PDA will be supported through:

a rolling delivery programme maintained through the JDT, responding to mayoral priorities, interventions and opportunities requiring joint action

a detailed annual Delivery Plan, agreed following approval of the PDA, translating strategic priorities into specific actions, responsibilities, milestones and resource commitments

an annual review process to refresh delivery priorities, resource allocations and pipeline activity without requiring the full PDA to be renegotiated

regular monitoring and performance reporting through the governance and accountability arrangements within this PDA, enabling partners to track progress, identify emerging risks and agree corrective action where required

The parties acknowledge that successful delivery will require ongoing collaboration between Homes England, the National Housing Bank, SYMCA and wider delivery partners, including local authorities, government departments, infrastructure providers, registered providers, investors and other stakeholders.

4.2 Joint Delivery Team (JDT)

The purpose of the South Yorkshire JDT will be to combine the collective resources of Homes England, National Housing Bank and SYMCA by providing additional capacity and capabilities to drive implementation of agreed priorities.

The functions of the South Yorkshire JDT will cover:

project and programme management

pipeline development

opportunity identification

investment co-ordination

land acquisition and remediation

risk management

performance monitoring

The JDT will take an integrated funding approach, bringing together the range of tools at our collective disposal where appropriate (including SAHP, NHDF, the South Yorkshire Housing Accelerator Fund, Mayoral Revolving Growth Fund and the National Housing Bank). This approach would also seek to bring in other Public Financial Institutions (PuFIns).

The JDT will be complemented by housing delivery expertise from across the wider Agency shaped to develop products, schemes and initiatives as part of this thematic capability, including on:

social and affordable housing

National Housing Bank finance and product specialists

specialist technical capabilities

strategy, research and innovation capacity

4.3 Governance and accountability

The Governance Framework will be developed further through the Delivery Plan and will include:

creating significantly enhanced accountability through a shared performance framework and direct reporting arrangements to the Mayor

establishing strengthened oversight arrangements involving the Mayor, the chairs of Homes England and the National Housing Bank and the chief executives of both organisations

introducing quarterly senior sponsor meetings to oversee delivery, resolve barriers and hold the partnership to account for agreed outcomes

In recognition of the commitment to create an even more responsive and re-wired delivery body as outlined in the Housing Minister’s letter, and to bring decision-making and accountability closer to impacted communities, the parties will commit in parallel to review existing delegations, reporting and accountability frameworks. Communications and stakeholder engagement activity will similarly be reviewed to maximise Homes England impact. Homes England will ensure information on planned activity within the geographical area of South Yorkshire will be shared with SYMCA in advance via the JDT.

Political oversight — South Yorkshire Mayor (in liaison with SPP Board) and reporting to SYMCA Board as appropriate.

Purpose — Strategic direction.

Strategic Leadership — Strategic Partnership Board: Quarterly.

Purpose — Oversight of PDA commitments and programme performance.

Executive Leadership — SYMCA Housing and Planning Director and Homes England Executive Regional Director.

Purpose — Executive oversight and resolution of major issues.

Joint Delivery Team — Weekly engagement.

Purpose — Delivery management, pipeline development and issue escalation.

In South Yorkshire there are specific place-based governance arrangements which will feed in and support this governance structure. This includes project-specific boards and the Sheffield Together Housing Growth Board. Where other local authorities wish to establish such strategic boards the JDT would seek to support these.

4.4 Resourcing

4.4.1 Resourcing — revenue

Homes England — Revenue support of £340,000, via a dedicated place budget, has been made available throughout the financial year April 2026 to March 2027, to help advance projects across South Yorkshire. Further funding will be identified in future years to support PDA delivery, subject to availability and approval.

SYMCA — A revenue budget of £1.5 million is available across the 15 NHDF mini-programmes that will support the development of business cases for the NHDF schemes.

£1.072 million of Council Housebuilding Support Fund has previously been provided to the 4 local authorities to accelerate council housing building schemes and further funding will also be available, subject to successful bids from the local authorities.

5. Implementation

The PDA will operate over a 3 year period and be reviewed annually.

Delivery will be supported through:

a rolling delivery programme maintained by the Joint Delivery Team

a detailed Delivery Business Plan agreed following PDA approval, setting out specific actions, responsibilities and milestones

an annual review of priorities, resources and pipeline activity without requiring the full PDA to be redrafted

regular performance reporting through the agreed governance structure

5.1 Delivery Plan

The PDA will be supported by a detailed Delivery Plan which will provide the primary mechanism for co-ordinating delivery activity and monitoring progress against agreed commitments.

The Delivery Plan will:

translate PDA strategic priorities and commitments into deliverable programmes, projects and interventions

set out milestones, outputs, funding requirements, resource commitments and dependencies

identify risks, constraints and barriers to delivery, together with proposed mitigation measures and required decisions

establish performance measures, success indicators and reporting arrangements

maintain a forward pipeline of opportunities and activities to support delivery of shared priorities

identify areas where additional collaboration, investment or intervention may be required to achieve agreed outcomes

Each partnership commitment included within the Delivery Plan will identify:

the agreed commitment or activity

the responsible organisation or organisations

a named lead owner

target completion or review dates

expected outputs and outcomes

success measures and monitoring arrangements

Following approval of the PDA, the JDU will co-ordinate preparation of the Delivery Plan and maintain it as a live document throughout the life of the PDA.

At PDA approval, partners will agree:

the timetable for preparation of the Delivery Plan

the lead organisation responsible for co-ordinating drafting and updates

governance arrangements for review, endorsement and approval

the senior officers authorised to approve revisions and updates

reporting arrangements to support effective oversight and accountability

The JDT will co-ordinate preparation of the Delivery Plan and maintain it as a live document throughout the life of the PDA.

5.2 Annual review

The PDA will be subject to an annual review led by the JDT and overseen through the governance arrangements referred to in this PDA. It will report to the Mayor and the Chief Executive and Chair of Homes England.

The review will:

assess progress against the commitments and success measures set out in the Delivery Plan

consider emerging opportunities, risks and policy developments

review resource requirements and delivery capacity

refresh the rolling programme of activity and priority projects

recommend amendments to the Delivery Plan where required

Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, changes arising through the annual review process will be managed through updates to the Delivery Plan and will not require the PDA itself to be redrafted or re-executed.

This approach will ensure that the PDA remains a stable long-term framework while enabling partners to adapt delivery activity in response to changing circumstances and opportunities.

6. General

The schedule to this PDA is incorporated into and forms part of this PDA.

This PDA shall not create the relationship of partnership joint venture and, or, agent relationships between the Parties, nor authorise the parties to make or enter into any commitments for or on behalf of another party.

Schedule

1. Confidentiality

1.1 In this clause the following words and expressions have the following meaning:

Confidential Information means the terms of this PDA and all information whether oral or written (on whatever medium stored) relating to this PDA disclosed or made available, directly or indirectly by one party or its employees, officers, representatives or advisers to the other party or its employees, officers, representatives or advisers but excludes any information which:

(i) at the time of such disclosure is, or subsequently becomes, publicly available;

(ii) at the time of such disclosure is, or subsequently becomes, available to the Recipient from a person who, to the Recipient’s knowledge, is not under any confidential obligation in respect of that information; or

(iii) has been independently acquired by a Party without breaching any of their respective obligations in this PDA.

1.2 Each Party recognises that under this PDA it may receive Confidential Information belonging to the other.

1.3 Each Party agrees to treat all Confidential Information belonging to the other as confidential and not to disclose such Confidential Information or any other confidential information relating to each other arising or coming to its attention in the course of this PDA to any third party without the prior written consent of the other Party and agrees not to use such Confidential Information for any purpose other than that for which it is supplied under this PDA.

1.4 The obligations of confidence referred to in Clause 1.3 shall not apply to any Confidential Information which:

(a) is in, or which comes into, the public domain otherwise than by reason of a breach of this PDA or of any other duty of confidentiality relating to that information; or

(b) is obtained from a third party without that third party being under an obligation (express or implied) to keep the information confidential; or

(c) is lawfully in the possession of the other Party before the date of this PDA and in respect of which that Party is not under an existing obligation of confidentiality; or

(d) is independently developed without access to the Confidential Information of the other Party.

1.5 Each Party will be permitted to disclose Confidential Information to the extent that it is required to do so:

(a) to enable the disclosing party to perform its obligations under this PDA; or by any applicable law or by a court, arbitral or administrative tribunal in the course of proceedings before it including without limitation any requirement for disclosure under Freedom of Information Laws (as defined in clause 2) and the Parties acknowledge that any lists or schedules provided by it outlining Confidential Information are of indicative value only and that the other party may nevertheless be obliged to disclose such confidential information; or

(b) by any regulatory body (including any investment exchange) acting in the course of proceedings before it or acting in the course of its duties; or

(c) in order to give proper instructions to any professional adviser of that Party who also has an obligation to keep any such Confidential Information confidential.

1.6 The Parties shall ensure that all Confidential Information obtained from the other Party under or in connection with this PDA:

(a) is given only to such of its employees, professional advisors or consultants engaged to advise it in connection with this PDA as is strictly necessary for the performance of this PDA and only to the extent necessary for the performance of this PDA;

(b) is treated as confidential and not disclosed (without Homes England’s prior written approval) or used by any such staff or professional advisors or consultants otherwise than for the purposes of this PDA and in all instances such third parties are subject to a signed confidentiality undertaking.

1.7 Notwithstanding any other provision of this PDA, nothing in this agreement shall prevent Homes England:

(a) disclosing any Confidential Information for the purpose of:

(i) the examination and certification of its accounts; or

(ii) any examination pursuant to section 6(1) of the National Audit Act 1983 of the economy, efficiency and effectiveness with which Homes England has used its resources; or

(b) disclosing any Confidential Information to any other department, office or agency of the Crown provided that in disclosing such Confidential Information pursuant to this paragraph (b), it discloses only the information which is necessary for the purpose concerned and requires that the information is treated in confidence.

1.8 Save as otherwise set out in this clause 1, no Party shall, and each Party shall use reasonable endeavours to ensure that no contractor, officer, employee or agent shall, communicate with any representative of any press, television, radio or other communications media on any matter concerning this PDA without the other Party’s prior written consent (in each case, not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed).

2. Freedom of Information

2.1 In this clause the following words and expressions have the following meaning:

Freedom of Information Laws means the Freedom of Information Act 2000 and the Environmental Information Regulations 2004 and any subordinate legislation made thereunder from time to time together with any guidance and, or, codes of practice issued by the Information Commissioner in relation to such legislation;

2.2 The Parties are each a public authority as defined under the Freedom of Information Laws and so may be required to disclose information in response to a request for information under those laws (Request for Information). The Party in receipt of a Request for Information (Recipient) shall be responsible for determining whether any such information insofar as it relates to this Agreement should be disclosed pursuant to a Request for Information and will:

(a) where appropriate and as soon as reasonably practicable inform the other Party that it has received a request to disclose information in response to a request for information under the Freedom of Information Laws; and

(b) in relation to such information and pursuant to the Freedom of Information Laws, consider the application of the exceptions and exemptions to disclosure before complying with any obligation to disclose such information.

2.3 Nothing in this PDA will prevent any Party from complying with any valid order, decision, enforcement or practice recommendation notice issued to it by the Information Commissioner under the Freedom of Information Laws.

3. Anti bribery

3.1 The Parties shall:

(a) comply with all applicable laws, statutes, regulations, and codes relating to anti-bribery and anti-corruption including but not limited to the Bribery Act 2010 (Requirements);

(b) not engage in any activity, practice or conduct which would constitute an offence under sections 1, 2 or 6 of the Bribery Act 2010 if such activity, practice or conduct had been carried out in the UK;

(c) have and maintain in place throughout the term of this PDA their own policies and procedures, including but not limited to adequate procedures under the Bribery Act 2010, to ensure compliance with the Requirements, the Relevant Policies and paragraph (b), and will enforce them where appropriate;

3.2 The Parties shall ensure that any person who is performing services or providing goods in connection with this Agreement does so only on the basis of a written contract which imposes on and secures from such person obligations in the same terms as paragraphs (a) to (c) above and also an obligation to immediately report to the appointing party any request or demand for any undue financial or other advantage of any kind received by them in connection with the performance of such services or the provision of such goods and to (at the request of the appointing party) produce a written certificate confirming compliance with the anti-bribery requirements and to provide such supporting evidence of compliance as the appointing party may reasonably request.

4. General

4.1 All individuals assigned by a Party to this PDA (each an Employer) to support the strategic priorities as identified in section 3 to this PDA and, or, the Delivery Plan shall remain employees of their Employer at all times. The Employer shall retain sole and exclusive responsibility for all employment-related matters pertaining to their assigned individuals. No provision of this Agreement shall be interpreted as creating any employment, agency, or partnership relationship between such Party’s individuals and the other Party to this PDA.

4.2 The Parties shall at all times act in good faith in relation to this PDA and enter into this PDA intending to honour all their obligations.

4.3 This PDA shall not create the relationship of partnership joint venture and, or, agent relationships between the Parties, nor authorise the parties to make or enter into any commitments for or on behalf of another party.

5. Status

5.1 This PDA is not intended to be legally binding, and no legal obligations or legal rights shall arise between the parties from this PDA.

5.2 The parties agree that clause 1 (Confidentiality) and clause 2 (Freedom of Information) are intended to be (and are) legally binding on each of them.
